phase1_leaf_result.tested_scope: Self-local deterministic replay comparing exactly three zero-cost repository-native acceptance-time fencing designs for generation-scoped create-once outputs under five scenarios: stale writer after pointer takeover, duplicate retry, pointer takeover race, ABA/reused-generation defense using a non-reusable claim epoch, and interruption after output creation but before acceptance. Design A was consumer re-read-and-reject; Design B was a single authoritative path whose CAS atomically validates the current non-reusable epoch and records effect acceptance; Design C was append-only output plus a separate accepted-effects pointer. No live claim mutation, public-source read, external coordinator, other-worker state, O/downstream input, or hosted compute was used.
observations: Design A rejects an output from an old epoch when the consumer re-reads the active pointer after takeover, but it remains vulnerable to a TOCTOU window if takeover occurs after that re-read and before the consumer commits the accepted effect; it also does not by itself serialize duplicate consumer acceptance.

Design B rejects a stale writer because takeover changes the authoritative path blob/epoch and the stale acceptance CAS fails. A duplicate retry is idempotent when the effect id/digest is already recorded on that path. Interruption after output creation but before acceptance leaves only an unaccepted orphan output; a later retry can safely attempt the acceptance CAS.

Design B is ABA-safe for the tested lineage only when the claim epoch is globally non-reusable and included in the authoritative path state. Under that condition an old logical generation cannot become current again, so an old acceptance precondition cannot become valid merely by generation-number reuse.

Design C prevents duplicate acceptance within the accepted-effects pointer when that pointer uses CAS/set semantics, but when active-epoch authority and accepted-effects state remain on separate paths, takeover can race between the active-pointer check and the accepted-effects CAS. The stale effect may therefore be recorded as accepted unless downstream consumers re-fence against the current epoch.

If Design C is changed so one authoritative path contains both the current non-reusable epoch and accepted-effect set and acceptance is one CAS on that path, its safety behavior collapses to Design B rather than remaining a distinct two-path protocol.
phase1_leaf_result.inference: Among the three tested designs, the single-path acceptance CAS is the strongest zero-hosted-coordination pattern for this exact scope because it combines takeover fencing and duplicate-acceptance idempotency in one repository-native CAS/readback boundary. Consumer re-read alone is insufficient without an atomic commit fence, and a separate accepted-effects pointer retains a cross-path race unless it is unified with current-epoch authority. This does not prove full multi-agent coordination parity or prevent stale output creation; it narrows the required acceptance invariant to non-reusable epoch plus single-path acceptance-time CAS.
phase1_leaf_result.unresolved_child: Test the single-path non-reusable-epoch acceptance CAS under multi-effect batching and takeover recovery, including two distinct effects racing with takeover, CAS conflict followed by next-invocation replay, and orphan-output garbage-collection policy that never mistakes unaccepted output existence for effect commitment.
